public_rationale: Stack Overflow's original policy provides substantial contemporary evidence of recurring incorrect answers in programming submissions. It supports part of Marcus's observation. It does not distinguish fabrication from other mistakes or establish the prevalence across ChatGPT's output generally. The verified records therefore do not settle the full frequency claim.
limitations: This does not mean fabrication was absent or rare.
Moderators' observations were qualitative and concerned a selected use case.
A narrower claim about frequent incorrect programming submissions would have stronger support.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: ChatGPT regularly makes things up and a fair amount of its output is false.

statement.excerpt: Which is to say it makes stuff up, regularly; a fair bit of what it is says simply isn’t true.
statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-4

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is recurring fabrication and a nontrivial amount of false factual content, rather than merely the possibility of an occasional error.
No exact percentage or majority threshold is supplied or imposed.
The target period is the initial public release through the post date, reflecting the post's current-state discussion.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary evaluations or well-documented observations establish recurring fabrication and materially frequent false factual content across ordinary uses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporary evaluations show that fabrication is exceptional and false factual content is negligible.
